summary: Independent r2 quality/security review of 00346416144c0e42897b79129be2021908830d1d: all three 33GOD-51 findings (F001 disjoint typed project root, F002 explicit-null service tier, F003 cleanup-failure precedence) are correctly fixed with no critical or important introduced defect. Fresh executions in this worktree: 42/42 focused contractor tests pass, Ruff clean on the three changed files, 24/24 neighboring service-tier/turn-config tests pass, and my own rerun of the eight differential node IDs under the locked review interpreter produced exact node-ID/error-class identity between head and immutable base (2 AssertionError failures and 6 passes at both revisions; zero branch-only, zero base-only, zero error-class changes). Hash verification confirms the preserved RED/GREEN/full-suite/differential logs match the implementation handback. Scope is exactly the three allowed files with one additive repair commit, remote branch verified at head, and both worktrees clean after all checks.

gateway/run.py _handle_contractor_turn (21274-21315 at head) validates context type, internal event, exact profile equality, command identity, then strict-resolves profile_home and project_root independently with is_dir checks before any skill load or executor dispatch; the defective is_relative_to(profile_home) containment rejection (red.log then-line 21302) is removed.

_resolve_turn_agent_config now defaults service_tier to the pre-existing gateway.session_state.SERVICE_TIER_UNSET sentinel and falls back to runner state only on omission (run.py:9060, 9114-9115); all three callers verified (6111 and 25963 omit and keep legacy fallback; 21148 contractor passes the locally resolved tier explicitly).

Post-success cleanup failure raises ContractorTurnCleanupFailed (run.py:2470-2471, 21412-21416); primary-failure path re-raises ContractorTurnRejected with the cleanup note attached via add_note (run.py:21404-21411); worker finally attaches the note to any in-flight exception via sys.exc_info (run.py:21257-21262).
Hash-verified RED log shows the five intended failures on the pre-repair tree for the exact behavioral reasons; hash-verified GREEN log shows 42 passed.
dimensions.assessment: The repair precisely targets the three confirmed defects without collateral behavior change. Validation order is correct (type, internal, profile, identity, then filesystem facts before skills/model/tools), the sentinel correctly separates explicit null from omission, and cleanup-error propagation preserves the primary exception in every branch. Fresh focused runs in this review worktree reproduce the GREEN state.

evidence: ContractorTurnContext is a frozen dataclass (gateway/platforms/base.py:2513-2564) whose __post_init__ rejects empty/unstripped contractor_id and profile_name, bool or non-positive contractor_version (type(v) is not int), memory_policy other than exactly 'none', continuity other than exactly False, non-tuple/empty/duplicate/unstripped required_skills, and non-absolute or non-resolving project_root; project_root is strict-resolved (symlinks fully resolved) and must be an existing directory at construction.

Handler-side revalidation (run.py:21294-21315) strict-resolves both roots again at dispatch time, closing the TOCTOU window between Bloodbank construction and Hermes execution; test_contractor_turn_revalidates_project_directory_before_skills[missing|file] proves failure before skill loading.

Fail-closed memory/tool invariants: disabled_toolsets forcibly gains memory and session_search (run.py:21112-21116), agent constructed with session_db=None, skip_memory=True, gateway_session_key=None, _persist_disabled=True, memory_notifications='off', and any residual memory state or memory/history-shaped tool raises ContractorTurnRejected before the first model call (run.py:21189-21213).

Cleanup warning logs only session_id and the cleanup exception (run.py:21252-21255) — no credentials, prompts, or secret material; no new env vars, no new dependencies (pyproject.toml and uv.lock untouched across the full range).
Only comments/docstrings mention Bloodbank in the full-range diff; grep confirms no bloodbank import in changed files, and no new imports were added to gateway/run.py at all.
dimensions.assessment: Type confusion, widening values, symlink escapes, and stale-path TOCTOU are all closed at both construction and dispatch boundaries. memory:none is enforced structurally and verified before model execution. Logging is minimal and secret-free. No new attack surface, dependency, or credential path is introduced.

evidence: ContractorTurnContext docstring (base.py:2515-2520) explicitly assigns registry resolution and pinning to the Bloodbank adapter; the run.py comment (21288-21293) states Hermes revalidates existence/type and deliberately does not duplicate registry authority via directory containment.

Bloodbank consumer seam (bloodbank/services/hermes-gateway/bloodbank_hermes_gateway/adapter.py) confirms the ownership split: it owns the fleet registry path (line 149-163 ProfileResolver), re-reads the route after pre-dispatch awaits (line 501-504 _assert_dispatch_route), journals execution, and maps ProcessingOutcome to terminal events in on_processing_complete (654-682); it constructs MessageEvent with keyword args and is unaffected by the appended contractor_context field.

Hermes-side authorization is not weakened by removing containment: unregistered routed targets are dropped via ProfileRouteRejected before contractor dispatch (run.py:31648-31654, 18881-18886), and the contractor handler requires exact source.profile == context.profile_name equality (run.py:21278-21282) plus event.internal is True (21276-21277).

The removed is_relative_to(profile_home) check was itself the F001 defect — it rejected the live, registry-authorized disjoint 33god-pm route (project /home/delorenj/code/33GOD vs profile ~/.hermes/profiles/33god-pm); containment was never the real authority, and keeping it would have been the directory-containment trust shortcut the acceptance criteria prohibit.
No callback/clone architecture and no second writable-root authority was introduced; cwd passed to the session scope is the strict-resolved project_root string (run.py:21337).
dimensions.assessment: The trust boundary is correctly placed: Bloodbank owns authenticated wire validation, registry root resolution, and canonicalization; Hermes owns process-local type and filesystem revalidation. Removing the containment check fixes a real false rejection without creating an authorization gap, because route authorization and profile equality are enforced upstream of and inside the handler. The two codebases' contracts are consistent and compatible.

evidence: The contractor worker keeps reasoning_config and service_tier in locals (run.py:21137-21150) and passes them as AIAgent constructor kwargs (21169-21171); grep of the worker range confirms zero writes to self._reasoning_config or self._service_tier.

Adapter-side state is reaped per stateless turn: base.py clear_session (6189-6199) removes _active_sessions/_pending_messages/_session_tasks/_post_delivery_callbacks and discards text debounce, invoked from the finished-task cleanup branch (7461-7466) only when close_after_turn or contractor_context is present, leaving ordinary sessions on the legacy _cleanup_finished_session_task path.

test_contractor_turn_does_not_mutate_shared_runner_state and test_concurrent_contractor_turns_leave_runner_config_unchanged pass at head, asserting runner._reasoning_config and runner._service_tier remain byte-identical after turns.
dimensions.assessment: Contractor turns cannot observe or mutate shared runner reasoning, tier, profile, session, memory, history, tool registry, or agent cache state. Isolation is enforced both by dispatch placement (before any session machinery) and by construction (fresh memoryless unpersisted agent), with adapter caches explicitly reaped after the turn.

evidence: _contractor_agents is guarded by _contractor_agents_lock (run.py:7701-7702) with getattr-based lazy init safe for object.__new__ test runners (21080-21096); registration is evicted in the worker finally (21247-21248) and both eviction tests pass at head.

Cancellation: the async CancelledError path sets the worker's cancel_event and requests a hard interrupt via _interrupt_contractor_agent before re-raising (run.py:21389-21392); the worker checks the event before construction and again after registration before the first model request (21099-21102, 21174-21179).

test_cancellation_signals_worker_before_requesting_hard_interrupt and test_cancelled_worker_stops_before_agent_construction pass at head, proving signal-before-interrupt ordering and pre-construction abort.

The platform finally cleanup still runs exactly once per turn; the contractor clear_session branch executes in the same owner-checked finally that guards ordinary sessions (base.py:7457-7466), so cancellation cannot double-clear or leak session tasks.
dimensions.assessment: Concurrent siblings are isolated by per-turn locals, per-turn session ids, and a locked registry; cancellation interrupts deterministically (event then hard interrupt) and cleanup runs exactly once via the worker finally plus the owner-checked platform finally. No cancellation regression versus the pre-contractor baseline behavior.

evidence: _cleanup_agent_resources now collects per-step errors and, with reraise=True (used only by the contractor path), raises the first error after all steps ran (run.py:12394-12463); default callers keep the legacy swallow-and-continue behavior, so no non-contractor path changed semantics.

Worker finally: cleanup failure during an in-flight primary exception is attached via active_exc.add_note and logged, never masking the primary (run.py:21247-21264); test_contractor_cleanup_failure_is_observed_on_failed_turn passes (primary RuntimeError 'model call failed' survives with cleanup note).

dimensions.assessment: Cleanup-error precedence is correct in all three orderings: post-success cleanup failure becomes the contractor failure (visible across the Bloodbank contract as FAILURE), cleanup failure during primary failure is attached without masking, and cancellation still unwinds through the same exactly-once finally. The F003 defect class is fully closed, not just the reported site.

findings.title: Module-level Slack adapter import makes Discord tests uncollectable without aiohttp installed
findings.description: The test module imports plugins.platforms.slack.adapter at module scope (line 296), and that adapter does a module-level 'import aiohttp' (adapter.py:23). In minimal environments without aiohttp (such as this review's locked venv), collection of the entire module fails — including the Discord-only TestDiscordMultiImage tests, which themselves inject a fake aiohttp via monkeypatch and never need the real package. This is pre-existing (the file is unchanged by the reviewed range) and symmetric across head and base, so it has no bearing on the differential verdict; I collected the mandatory node with a disclosed per-invocation PYTHONPATH shim instead of installing anything.
findings.impact: Environment friction only: in dependency-minimal environments the eight-node differential requires a shim or a fuller venv; no runtime, security, or correctness impact, and the node outcome was identical at both revisions in three independent environments.
findings.required_fix: No fix required for this change. Optional hardening outside this story's scope: gate the module-level Slack import (or make the Slack adapter's aiohttp import lazy) so Discord-focused tests collect without aiohttp installed.
